observed_discontinuity: Frozen Bubble GameScreen.paint calls Vector.size and then Vector.elementAt. The game VM had no Ljava/util/Vector;, so new-instance fell back to Object and the invokes were skipped. Earlier Vector.<init>, addElement, and removeElement on the same startup were also skipped, so a fabricated empty size would hide the sprites.
required_semantics: Vector() allocates elementData with length DEFAULT_SIZE 10, elementCount 0, and capacityIncrement 0. The constructor is not synchronized.
addElement appends the object and grows by doubling when capacityIncrement is 0 and the array is full.
elementAt returns the stored object at a valid index.
elementAt throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when the index is outside 0 inclusive through size exclusive.
removeElement removes the first element for which equals is true, shifts the later elements down, and returns true. A missing element returns false.
size, addElement, elementAt, and removeElement synchronize on the Vector.

differences.description: Ljava/util/Vector; was not a guest class. Construction fell back to Object, and size, addElement, removeElement, and elementAt were unresolved.
differences.relevance: GameScreen.paint reads sprites.size and sprites.elementAt. Those reads depend on the earlier Vector.<init>, removeElement, and addElement calls that build the same Vector.

earliest_evidenced_divergence: API19 Vector stores guest objects in elementData and size returns elementCount. AGR skipped every Vector invoke, so GameScreen.paint never received the stored Sprite.

evidence.artifact: android-4.4.4_r2 libcore luni java.util.Vector. DEFAULT_SIZE is 10. Vector() calls Vector(10, 0) and is not synchronized. size returns elementCount. addElement appends and calls growByOne when full. growByOne doubles the array when capacityIncrement is 0. elementAt returns elementData[location] when location < elementCount, otherwise arrayIndexOutOfBoundsException(location, elementCount), which throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException(size, index). removeElement uses indexOf, which uses equals or null identity, then removeElementAt shifts the tail and clears the vacated slot.

Linux vector-core-host PASS. Vector() size is 0. addElement A then B then C yields size 3 and elementAt identity A, B, C. elementAt(size) and elementAt(-1) throw Ljava/lang/ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; and size stays 3. removeElement B returns true, size becomes 2, and elementAt(1) is C. A missing remove returns false. Null is stored, returned, and removed. Twelve further appends grow past 10 and elementAt(13) is the same object.

remaining_uncertainty: elementAt of a negative index throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException with the helper message length and index. API19 reaches the array when the index is negative and elementCount is positive, so the exception class matches and the message can differ.
equals falls back to reference identity unless the key class defines an equals method other than Object.equals.
modCount is not stored. Enumeration, iterator, insertElementAt, and the rest of Vector are not registered.
Activity.requestWindowFeature is outside this Vector contract. It is resolved separately and was not a proven blocker.
next_action: java.util.Vector core stays REAL_GAME_CONFIRMED for Vector(), size, addElement, removeElement, and elementAt. Do not reopen Vector. Do not rerun the content-frame Simulator.
host_adaptation: Vector is a guest class extending Object, with elementData, elementCount, and capacityIncrement. elementData is a guest object array, so the existing GC field and array walk keeps the elements alive. Public methods take the Vector monitor. This is not ArrayList.
